#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 3 -n 96 -t 30m --job-name=EQ_POCG_60 --output=starting.out script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 3         : 3 nodes (from -N 3)
# -n 96        : 96 tasks (from -n 96)
# -t 30m       : 30 minute walltime (from -t 00:30:00)
# --job-name=EQ_POCG_60 : job name (from -J EQ_POCG_60)
# --output=starting.out : output file (from --output=starting.out)
#
# Note: The original has conflicting --output directives:
# - out%j.amarel.log (with job ID)
# - starting.out (fixed name)
# Using starting.out as it appears last and would override

# Alternative resource configuration (commented out in original):
# -N 1 -n 32  : 1 node with 32 tasks

# Memory: 6000 MB (--mem=6000)
# Note: Flux memory specification varies by version
# Add to submission command: --setattr=system.memory=6000M
# Or: --setattr=memory=6000M (verify for your Flux version)
# Complete command:
# flux batch -N 3 -n 96 -t 30m --setattr=system.memory=6000M --job-name=EQ_POCG_60 --output=starting.out script.sh
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory request, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient for NAMD molecular dynamics simulation

# Export environment: --export=ALL
# Slurm: --export=ALL exports all environment variables
# Note: Flux batch jobs inherit the environment from submission shell by default
# Performance impact: Environment inheritance behavior similar
# If specific environment control is needed, use --env or --env-remove at submission

# Partition: cmain
# Slurm: --partition=cmain
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Partition selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or queues

# Requeue: --requeue
# Slurm: --requeue allows automatic requeue on node failure
# Note: Flux does not have a direct --requeue equivalent
# Flux handles job failure and restart differently through its job management
# Performance impact: Jobs will not automatically requeue on node failure
# Consider implementing application-level checkpointing for fault tolerance
# Or use Flux's job exception handling mechanisms if available

# Output file disambiguation:
# Original has two --output directives:
# 1. -o out%j.amarel.log (with job ID placeholder %j)
# 2. --output=starting.out (fixed filename)
# Slurm would use the last one (starting.out)
# Flux: --output=starting.out (fixed name, no job ID)
# To include job ID in Flux: --output=out{{id}}.amarel.log
# Current conversion uses starting.out to match original behavior

# Module environment
module purge
module load gcc cuda mvapich2/2.2

# Application paths
NAMD="/projects/jdb252_1/tj227/bin/namd2-2.13-gcc-mvapich2"

# MPI launcher
# Original: SRUN="srun --mpi=pmi2"
# Slurm: srun with PMI2 process management interface
# Flux: Use flux run for launching MPI tasks
# PMI2 support in Flux depends on MPI implementation and configuration
# MVAPICH2 typically supports PMI/PMI2
# Flux equivalent:
FLUX_RUN="flux run -n 96"

# Execute NAMD simulation
# Original: $SRUN $NAMD starting.POCG_60.namd > starting.POCG_60.log
# Flux: flux run launches MPI tasks within the allocation
$FLUX_RUN $NAMD starting.POCG_60.namd > starting.POCG_60.log

# Note on MPI execution:
# - flux run is used instead of srun
# - -n 96 specifies 96 MPI tasks (matching the allocation)
# - Flux will distribute tasks across the 3 allocated nodes
# - MVAPICH2 should work with Flux's PMI implementation
# - If PMI2 is specifically required, ensure MVAPICH2 is built with Flux PMI support
# - For explicit node distribution, use: flux run -N 3 -n 96

# Complete submission command with all options:
# flux batch -N 3 -n 96 -t 30m \
#   --setattr=system.memory=6000M \
#   --job-name=EQ_POCG_60 \
#   --output=starting.out \
#   script.sh
#
# Or with job ID in output:
# flux batch -N 3 -n 96 -t 30m \
#   --setattr=system.memory=6000M \
#   --job-name=EQ_POCG_60 \
#   --output=out{{id}}.amarel.log \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory specification is documented but not included in the primary submission command at the top. The primary command should be: 'flux batch -N 3 -n 96 -t 30m --setattr=system.memory=6000M --job-name=EQ_POCG_60 --output=starting.out script.sh'

The memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory=6000M' should be verified for the specific Flux version. Alternative syntax '--setattr=memory=6000M' may be needed depending on the Flux installation.

The 'flux run' command inside the script specifies '-n 96' which matches the batch allocation, but this is redundant. When running inside a batch job with 96 tasks allocated, 'flux run' without '-n' would use all allocated tasks by default. However, explicit specification is acceptable and makes intent clear.

The memory allocation of 6000MB (approximately 6GB) total across 3 nodes for 96 tasks results in only ~62.5MB per task. This may be insufficient for NAMD molecular dynamics simulations, which typically require more memory per process. Consider if this should be --mem-per-cpu or if the memory value needs to be increased.

The conversion correctly notes that Slurm's --mem=6000 is total memory for the job, but NAMD with 96 MPI ranks typically needs significantly more than 6GB total. Verify this memory specification meets application requirements.
No cores-per-task specification is provided. With 96 tasks on 3 nodes, this implies 32 tasks per node. Ensure nodes have sufficient cores to support this distribution (at least 32 cores per node).
The script does not specify any node-specific constraints or topology requirements. For multi-node NAMD jobs, network topology and node capabilities may affect performance.
The requeue behavior from Slurm is not replicated in Flux. For long-running molecular dynamics simulations, consider implementing checkpointing within NAMD to enable manual restart on failure.

Output redirection to 'starting.POCG_60.log' is done via shell redirection (>) rather than Flux's output handling. This means Flux's stdout/stderr capture (--output=starting.out) and the application's log file will be separate, which may be intentional but should be noted.
